markdown_report:
The best first step is a padding-audited, paired history-perturbation diagnostic for the supplied GRU4Rec. At 0% research progress, verify implementation correctness and temporal dependence before changing training. Perturbations generate hypotheses; validation HR@10 determines whether an intervention helps.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Positive–negative margins measure training separability. They cannot establish current intent; missing observations must return null with counts, not healthy-looking zeros.
2. Left padding can confound recurrent representations. Zero padding embeddings do not prevent recurrent updates; correctness requires explicit invariance tests.
3. Feedback suggests weak immediate relevance and redundancy. Histories and text support connection proxies, but cannot establish compatibility, mood or unwanted ownership duplication.

**Insights from related work**

1. *Measuring Recency Bias* [1] cautions against excessive recency emphasis. Greater sensitivity is not inherently better.
2. Recency-sampling research [2] supports a feasible subsequent GRU4Rec intervention. Its benefit on these four datasets remains untested.
3. Prakash et al. [3] motivate popularity strata; shuffled-history research [4] shows dataset-dependent sensitivity. Neither establishes that sensitivity predicts accuracy gains.

**Framework and candidate directions**

| Direction | Evidence produced | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation correctness | Padding invariance and correct readout | Does not establish relevance |
| Temporal dependence | Paired score/rank changes | Perturbations do not establish intent |
| Objective adaptation | Validation HR@10 after retraining | Gains may differ across categories |

Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Padding-audited paired perturbations [1,4] | 3 / 7 / 4 | Originality: + integrated controls, − established components. Potential: + guides hypotheses, − unvalidated intervention link. Difficulty: + existing hooks, − alignment and candidates require care. |
| Recent-window training sampling [2] | 3 / 7 / 4 | Originality: + task adaptation, − established technique. Potential: + localized change, − recency shortcuts possible. Difficulty: + sampler edit, − retraining required. |
| Popularity-stratified margin diagnosis [3] | 3 / 6 / 2 | Originality: + contextualized errors, − standard stratification. Potential: + exposes aggregate failures, − repairs nothing directly. Difficulty: + training counts suffice, − sparse strata are noisy. |

**Selected algorithm**

Compare equal-count oldest/latest deletion and older-item shuffling preserving the latest input. Set k=min(3,max(1,n//4)) for n≥2; skip ineligible cases. Freeze target, candidate IDs and original-history exclusions. Include repeat targets once and report repeat/nonrepeat strata separately from unseen-item recommendations.

```
for deterministic training diagnostic histories:
    audit padding, batch independence and predictor parity
    construct matched deletions and last-item-preserving shuffle
    encode variants using the same trained category GRU
    gather final nonpadding features using position indices
    score fixed candidates; accumulate paired changes
return metrics, metric_definitions
```

Define Δrank=perturbed−original and overlap@10=intersection size/10; positive Δrank indicates deterioration. Record score changes, final-state cosine distance, ties, counts, missingness and protocol details. Break diagnostic ties by descending score then ascending item ID. Sampled ranks are not full-catalog ranks [5]. Bootstrap paired user means within category; report training-derived popularity/history-length strata descriptively.

Preserve both diagnostic entry points and ModelView hooks. Compact, pack, unpack and restore timestep positions if correctness tests require repair [6]; synchronize training and predictor semantics. Use eval mode, zero initial states and bounded training-only probes. Training memorization and unrealistic shuffles limit interpretation. Keep one checkpoint/category; accept subsequent interventions only by pinned macro validation HR@10.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [5](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [6](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html).

idea.description: Add padding-invariance checks and matched history perturbations to the existing GRU4Rec diagnostic adapter, using the same independently trained model for every comparison within a category. Treat findings as evidence of model reliance and sources of intervention hypotheses, without assuming that sensitivity measures current intent or predicts accuracy improvements.
idea.motivation: Existing margins measure separability without revealing temporal dependence or implementation artifacts. Equal-count oldest-versus-newest deletion controls the amount of removed history, while last-item-preserving shuffling distinguishes dependence on older ordering from dependence on the final observed item. The integrated protocol has no supplied direct validation as a predictor of GRU4Rec improvements, so its originality and future-potential ratings are reduced and its implementation difficulty increased.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence) and predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; unavailable categories must produce empty category breakdowns with an availability explanation. Do not infer ratings, reviews, compatibility, mood, simulator traits or ownership needs.

Run the actual module in eval mode under no_grad and restore its previous mode in a finally block. Every independent history starts with zero recurrent state. Audit identical histories under different left-padding widths, batched versus individual execution, batch permutations, changed neighboring users, repeated calls after unrelated batches, timestep alignment, empty/single-item histories, and checkpoint-loaded predictor parity. Start FP32 comparisons at rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-6; record observed differences and justify any tolerance adjustment. No architecture or predictor change is needed only if these checks pass.

If padding handling fails, compact nonpadding items in their original order into right-padded rows, exclude empty histories, and use pack_padded_sequence with CPU lengths, batch_first=True and enforce_sorted=False. Unpack with total_length=L and scatter valid outputs back to original positions so log2feats remains B×L×H and aligns with positive/negative targets. Apply downstream transformations consistently. Define empty-row sequence features as zeros; exclude those rows from perturbation metrics. Train and write the embedded predictor using identical repaired semantics; retain only the selected single checkpoint per category. Repairs to training semantics require retraining before validation.

Use a bounded training diagnostic sample: at most ten loader batches and 256 distinct users per category, whichever limit is reached first. Obtain stable user and prefix identifiers through the existing family-specific sampler or a sidecar sampling manifest; keep the loader's four-element yield unchanged. Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42, with a separate diagnostic RNG seeded 42. Persist user/prefix identifiers and diagnostic draws beneath the trial directory. If user identifiers cannot be recovered, omit user-bootstrap intervals and explicitly report that limitation rather than treating prefixes as independent users.

For each nonempty row, select the maximum index where sequence is nonzero, never nonpadding-count minus one, and take the positive target aligned with that position. Exclude target zero. Define deletion count k=min(3,max(1,n//4)) for n>=2. Remove exactly k oldest versus k latest items. Shuffle all but the latest observed input with the diagnostic RNG; report histories with fewer than two older items, duplicate-induced unchanged shuffles, and other no-op cases separately. Reuse the same target after perturbation: this is a reliance test and may create implausible histories, not a counterfactual preference label.

For each original prefix, sample up to 99 unique negatives uniformly without replacement from valid training-catalog item IDs, excluding padding/reserved IDs, the target and the original observed history. Include the target exactly once, including when it appeared earlier in the history. Freeze candidate IDs and original-history exclusions across every variant; never make deleted items newly eligible. Record candidate IDs, requested/actual count, distribution, replacement policy, exclusions and seed. If fewer than 99 eligible negatives exist, use all eligible negatives and report candidate-count strata. Report repeat/nonrepeat target strata. Repeat-aware diagnostic targets remain separate from the simulator's strict unseen-item recommendation population, and benchmark rules remain unchanged.

Rank by descending score then ascending item ID using deterministic sorting. Define target rank as one plus the number of candidates preceding it. Define delta rank as perturbed rank minus original rank, delta target score as perturbed minus original score, overlap@10 as shared top-10 items divided by ten, and state distance as one minus final-feature cosine similarity. Return null overlap@10 for pools smaller than ten and null cosine distance for zero-norm features. Record exact target-score ties and ties crossing the top-10 boundary. These are sampled diagnostic ranks, not benchmark HR@10 or full-catalog positions.

Aggregate prefixes into user means, then compute paired category means and 95% percentile intervals from 1,000 user-bootstrap draws with seed 42. These intervals condition on fixed candidates and histories; they do not capture training-seed or candidate-sampling uncertainty. Use history-length bins 1, 2–5, 6–20 and 21+; define target-popularity bins by training-frequency item-rank thirds with ascending item ID as the tie-break. Report joint-stratum counts and avoid strong interpretations of sparse cells. Preserve original margin metrics and embedding diagnostics; return null with reasons when undefined rather than zeros.

Use training-only diagnostics to generate hypotheses, acknowledge prefix memorization, and avoid optimizing sensitivity as an objective. Random shuffles can violate catalog-availability constraints; do not call them realistic behavior or causal evidence. Any later availability-constrained probe must use training-only timestamp evidence and report unknown availability. Predeclare subsequent sampler interventions and compare them through the host's fixed macro validation HR@10; repeated validation selection can still overfit. If per-user validation outcomes are provided by the unchanged host, paired within-category bootstrap differences can describe uncertainty conditional on fixed evaluation candidates. Never read test labels.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Keep seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, fixed splits and the pinned evaluator. Do not read other trials, reuse checkpoints, fetch external data or weights, or introduce independent predictors, fusion or checkpoint averaging. Diagnostic passes and any necessary retraining consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        prior_mode = view.model.training
        view.model.eval()
        try:
            with no_grad():
                audit_padding_batch_state_alignment_and_predictor_parity()
                # Fail clearly if correctness is unresolved; repair/retrain separately.
                for batch, manifest in bounded_training_batches_and_sidecar_ids(
                        train_loader, max_batches=10, max_users=256):
                    _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
                    retain_existing_margin_and_embedding_probes()
                    for row in batch:
                        positions = indices_where(row.sequence != 0)
                        if positions.empty:
                            record_skip('empty_history')
                            continue
                        final_index = positions.max()
                        target = row.positive[final_index]
                        if target == 0:
                            record_skip('missing_target')
                            continue
                        history = row.sequence[positions]
                        candidates = persist_fixed_uniform_candidates(
                            target=target, negative_count=99,
                            exclusions=set(history) | reserved_ids,
                            retain_target_once=True, rng=diagnostic_rng_42)
                        if len(history) < 2:
                            record_skip('insufficient_history_for_deletion')
                            continue
                        k = min(3, max(1, len(history) // 4))
                        variants = {
                            'original': history,
                            'remove_oldest': history[k:],
                            'remove_latest': history[:-k],
                            'shuffle_older': shuffle(history[:-1], diagnostic_rng_42)
                                             + history[-1:]
                        }
                        for name, items in variants.items():
                            seq = left_pad(items)
                            features = view.log2feats(seq)  # fresh zero recurrent state
                            index = max_position_where(seq != 0)
                            final = gather_per_row(features, index)
                            scores = view.predict_score(final, candidates)
                            ranking = sort_by_desc_score_then_ascending_item_id(scores)
                            record(name, final, scores, ranking, target)
                        accumulate_paired_metrics_with_user_prefix_ids(manifest)
                aggregate_prefixes_to_users()
                bootstrap_user_means_if_ids_available(draws=1000, seed=42)
                return {'metrics': measured_results_counts_or_null,
                        'metric_definitions': definitions_protocol_and_limits}
        finally:
            view.model.train(prior_mode)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return interpretation_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        output_keys=['status', 'core_findings', 'key_implications', 'evidence'],
        require_metric_names_counts_and_uncertainty=True,
        distinguish_training_separability_from_validation_accuracy=True,
        forbid_unsupported_intent_compatibility_and_causal_claims=True)

originality.positive: The integration of matched deletions, last-item-preserving shuffles, padding controls and explicit eligibility handling provides a useful task-specific protocol.
originality.negative: Its components are established, and the supplied literature does not validate the complete combination as a novel predictor of GRU4Rec improvement.

future_potential.positive: A reproducible protocol can identify implementation failures and motivate focused GRU4Rec sampling or objective experiments across categories.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity can reflect memorization, catalog evolution or unrealistic perturbations; its connection to improved current-intent recommendations remains unproven.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing ModelView hooks permit most probes without adding a trained model or changing inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable implementation requires user-level bookkeeping, fixed eligibility, deterministic ties, uncertainty estimates and possible synchronized packing repairs in training and the predictor.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary reports that excessive emphasis on recent interactions can hurt recommendation accuracy.
Motivates measuring temporal dependence without treating stronger recency sensitivity as inherently better.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied GRU4Rec has excessive recency bias.
Does not validate history perturbations as measurements of current user intent.

related_work.title: Recency-sampling research involving GRU4Rec (2022)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes training-objective changes evaluated with GRU4Rec.
Provides a practical subsequent direction if diagnostics motivate changing training-example recency.
limitations: Transfer to the four pinned Amazon datasets remains untested.
Changing temporal sampling may improve some categories while hurting others.

related_work.title: Prakash et al.: sequential recommendation and popularity-dependent evaluation (2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary reports that aggregate metrics can conceal head, middle and tail item differences.
Motivates training-derived popularity strata when interpreting diagnostic margins and perturbation responses.
limitations: Popularity-stratified diagnostics do not directly establish subjective usefulness.
Diagnostic candidate sampling must remain separate from the pinned benchmark evaluator.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes shuffled-history evaluations of GRU4Rec and SASRec across 15 datasets using ranking metrics, recommendation overlap and bootstrap tests.
Supports examining dataset-dependent reliance on sequential order.
limitations: Observed sensitivity does not establish that increasing or decreasing it improves ordinary next-item accuracy.
Does not directly validate the complete matched-deletion and final-input-preserving protocol.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of evaluating item rankings through sampled candidate sets.
Supports explicit candidate protocols and separating sampled diagnostic ranks from full-catalog rankings.
limitations: Does not prescribe the best candidate distribution for these GRU4Rec diagnostics.
Fixed diagnostic candidates control a confound but do not guarantee full-catalog agreement.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Documents length-based packed recurrent inputs and automatic sorting with enforce_sorted=False.
Supports excluding padding from GRU recurrence after compacting nonpadding items.
limitations: Packing alone does not restore features to the original left-padded target positions.
Empty histories require explicit handling.

related_work.title: PyTorch pad_packed_sequence documentation
contributions: Documents unpacking with a specified total_length and restoring original batch order.
Supports reconstructing aligned B×L×H diagnostic and training features.
limitations: The implementation must still scatter compacted outputs to original nonpadding positions.
Downstream transformations and predictor serialization must preserve the same semantics.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Documents GRU recurrence and zero initial hidden states when h_0 is omitted.
Clarifies why padding embeddings alone do not suppress recurrent state updates.
limitations: Framework defaults cannot prevent application code from carrying hidden states between unrelated users.
The packed final hidden state is equivalent to a final recurrent output only before any additional downstream transformations.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy guidance
contributions: Explains why mathematically equivalent batched computations need not be bitwise identical.
Supports tolerance-based invariance and predictor-parity checks.
limitations: Provides no universal tolerance suitable for every backend and dtype.
Numerical tolerance must not conceal material padding or state-leakage errors.

related_work.title: PyTorch topk documentation
contributions: Warns that indices of tied elements are not guaranteed to be stable.
Motivates explicit score-then-item-ID ordering for reproducible diagnostic ranks and overlap.
limitations: Diagnostic tie handling must remain separate from the unchanged host evaluator.
Deterministic ordering does not remove uncertainty from tied scores.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (RecSys 2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary compares random shuffling with item-availability-constrained shuffling.
Highlights catalog evolution as a possible explanation for apparent sequential dependence.
limitations: Availability-constrained perturbations require sufficiently reliable timestamp and eligibility evidence.
Neither random nor constrained shuffling establishes current user intent or the correct training intervention.
